messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service 'inference-queue-consumer' (high 5xx rate on /v1/generate). Trigger: 5m error rate > 5%. PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-48291
Suresh: I'm taking this — acknowledging in PD now.
pd-bot: Suresh acknowledged incident PD-48291.
Maya: ping — what's the customer impact? any dedicated tenants affected?
Suresh: early triage: spike started ~23:10 UTC. EU region. Hosted API falling back intermittently; a few dedicated tenants report 500s. No obvious auth or DB errors.
Jon: looking at infra — kube events show frequent restarts on inference-consumer pods.
Jon: running quick check:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep consumer
# consumer-5d6f7  Running  3/5  1d  10.1.2.34
# consumer-6c7e8  CrashLoopBackOff  0/5  2m
```
Suresh: grabbing logs from a crashed pod:
```
journalctl -u inference-consumer -n 200 | grep -i "HTTP 500" | head -n 5
2025-11-02T23:12:14Z inference-consumer[pid=123] ERROR HTTP 500 model-serving connection reset by peer
2025-11-02T23:12:14Z inference-consumer[pid=123] ERROR kv-cache: grew beyond 2.1G
```
Tara: Ops-Lead — any quick mitigation suggestions? Could be memory blowup from KV cache growth.
Ops-Lead: Proposal: (1) scale up consumer replicas temporarily, (2) roll restart deployment to clear cache, (3) disable prefix caching flag for now to avoid regrowth while we investigate.
Maya: agree with comms plan: start notifying affected customers once we have ETA.
Suresh: performing a controlled restart of consumers and scaling replicas +2:
```
kubectl scale deploy/inference-consumer -n inference --replicas=8
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-consumer -n inference --timeout=600s
```
pd-bot: Suresh initiated scale and restart actions. PD note added.
Jon: looking at metrics: mem usage for consumer pods climbed steadily starting 23:08 UTC. Heap / cache accounted for it. I think the new KV-prefix caching change from last deploy is the culprit.
Suresh: temp mitigation — starting instance-level flag to disable kv-prefix cache to prevent regrowth:
```
kubectl set env deploy/inference-consumer -n inference KV_PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false
```
Suresh: also bumping autoscaler target temporarily to absorb traffic.
support-bot: Notifying support channel and creating incident ticket INC-2025-48291 for customer-facing comms.
Maya: drafted a short status for the status.redwood.ai page: "We are investigating elevated 500 errors for the inference API in EU. Mitigation in progress." Will post after Ops-Lead review.
Ops-Lead: Good. Assign follow-ups: Suresh for root-cause and rollback plan, Jon for metrics/postmortem, Maya for customer comms. I'll stay as bridge until handoff.
Jon: after scale + disable flag + restart, error rate dropped from ~8% to 0.9% in the past 4 minutes. Request latency also recovering.
Suresh: confirming logs post-restart:
```
journalctl -u inference-consumer -n 100 | grep -i "ERROR HTTP 500" | wc -l
2
```
Maya: posting to status page now. Linking customers via support ticket list.
pd-bot: PD incident PD-48291 updated: mitigation in place. Escalation auto-cleared.
Ops-Lead: ETA for monitoring window — keep this thread open for 15m stable window. If stable, Suresh should mark resolved and create a postmortem ticket with timeline + deploy diff.
Suresh: will mark resolved once stable for 15m. Opening follow-up: ENG-2431 "Investigate KV prefix cache leak after deploy".
Tara: quick note — no evidence of data exfiltration. Affected requests returned 500s only. Customer impact estimate: 3-7% of EU region requests for ~22 minutes.
Maya: support is sending an initial "we're investigating" note to affected tenants, will follow up after RMS.
Suresh: PD: marking incident resolved. Added mitigation steps and follow-ups to PD notes.
pd-bot: Incident PD-48291 resolved by Suresh. Duration: ~22m. Postmortem: ENG-2431.
incident-bot: Incident thread closed. Suggested postmortem owners: Suresh (primary), Jon (metrics), Maya (customer comms). Reaction: :white_check_mark:
Ops-Lead: Thanks team — good rapid triage. We'll run RCA tomorrow and schedule a canary rollback or patch. Closing this bridge for now.
Maya: grabbing the logs and will add customer-facing blurb to the support ticket. I'll ping when posted.
Suresh: final note — temporary mitigation (KV_PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false) will remain until patch. I will schedule a safe rollout with canary and memory profiler.
Jon: recording dashboards and saving metric windows to ENG dashboards library for the postmortem.
Maya: closing loop with support in 30m. :thumbsup:
